# Bakajātaka (Ja 38)
**ID:** Ja 38
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Bakajātaka

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Bakajātaka* (Ja 38) is a story in the Jātaka collection featuring the moral adage that guile does not profit the deceitful [SuttaCentral]. According to the *paccuppannavatthu* (introductory narrative), the Buddha related the story while residing at Jetavana with reference to a monk who was an expert robe-maker (*cīvaravaddhaka*); this monk deceptively fashioned old rags to look like fine cloth until he was outwitted by another tailoring monk from a village [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1877; von Hinüber, Everyday Life]. In the past story (*atītavatthu*), a deceptive crane tricks a pond of fish by offering to transport them to a safer pool, only to devour them one by one, until a crab seizes the crane by the neck with its pincer and kills it; the Bodhisatta was the tree deity (*rukkhadevatā*) who witnessed the crane's downfall and declared the concluding verse [Fausböll 1877; Luce et al. 1970].
Modern scholars have highlighted the technical terminology preserved in the introductory account of the monk's craft, which illuminates tailoring and dyeing practices in ancient Indian monasteries—such as cutting (*chedana*), smoothing (*ghaṭṭana*), measuring (*vicāraṇa*), sewing (*sibbana*), and re-dyeing cloth with paste-infused water (*piṭṭhodaka*) [Lamotte, Mahāyānasaṃgraha; Anacker 1984; von Hinüber, Everyday Life]. In later Buddhist discourse in Sri Lanka, Ja 38 has also been cited among canonical stories examined in discussions surrounding acceptable limits on conflict [Bartholomeusz 2002]. Art historically, the tale's climax—depicting the crab clamping the crane's neck—is attested on early Burmese terracotta plaques from sites such as Hpetleik in Pagan [Luce et al. 1970].
Neither SuttaCentral nor the DharmaNexus database records any direct canonical parallels or significant cross-language alignments (score ≥ 10) for this text [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
